target_customer: Makers and brands that wanted to take pre-orders and crowdfund on their own sites, often after a Kickstarter or Indiegogo campaign
problem: Creators finishing crowdfunding campaigns had no easy way to keep taking pre-orders and payments until products shipped.
business_model: Platform fee on pre-order and crowdfunding sales

founders.name: Chris Tsai
founders.background_notes: YC page lists as Founder/CEO with no bio.

founders.name: Peter Shih
founders.background_notes: YC bio: first engineer to VP of Engineering at Clarium.

founders.name: Brian Nguyen
founders.background_notes: YC page lists as Founder/CPO with no bio.

exit.reason: Indiegogo bought Celery's assets (domain, logo, source code licenses) and folded them into InDemand; reports said Celery stayed a standalone business through the transition.

technical_complexity.rationale: Payment authorization and deferred charging on a storefront is standard e-commerce engineering, with some difficulty in handling charge-at-ship flows.

defensibility.rationale: Merchants were embedded through their stores, but rivals and platforms like Indiegogo could copy a pre-order tool quickly.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Indiegogo launched its own InDemand pre-order product in January 2015 and then bought Celery's assets in May 2016.

market_need_then: Crowdfunded products had no clean path to continued pre-orders after campaigns ended, and TechCrunch (2013-05-21) covered Celery as a way to ride the crowdfunding wave.

branding.domain_note: Used trycelery.com with a try prefix, indicating celery.com was not used.

identity.voice_and_tone: Playful: Crowdfund Insider (2015-08) describes a launch video poking fun at cookie-cutter crowdfunding platforms.

brand_strength.rationale: Known in the crowdfunding niche and covered by TechCrunch, but no sourced mascot, community or merch; the real-word name competes with the vegetable in search.

pivots.to: Celery Launch, hosting crowdfunding or pre-order campaigns on the merchant's own site
pivots.why: Expand into campaigns run independently of Kickstarter and Indiegogo (Crowdfund Insider, 2015-08).

outcome_analysis: Celery rode the 2012 to 2015 crowdfunding wave with a pre-order tool for makers and raised a reported 2 million dollar seed in February 2014. Indiegogo shipped its own InDemand pre-order product in January 2015, which put the largest crowdfunding platform directly in its niche, and bought Celery's assets in May 2016. The company's stated cause for inactivity is that the product was absorbed into Indiegogo rather than a shutdown for lack of customers; reasons beyond that are not public.
notes: trycelery.com returned HTTP 503 when fetched. The 2.3M second 2014 round rests on a single database (ZoomInfo) and has no named investors or stage label. Totals conflict: ZoomInfo 4.3M, CB Insights 2.02M over 4 rounds, Seedtable 2.83M over 1 round (and a 381K figure). The YC description lists General Catalyst and Elementum as backers but no round for them was sourced. No competitor source dated near the Summer 2012 batch was found (the TechCrunch 2014 article names Shoplocket, too late), so the list is empty. Chris Tsai and Brian Nguyen are described as founders by a search summary; Peter Shih's bio comes from the YC page.
